newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian serial murder case takes fresh twist.
newsitem.headline: Italian serial murder case takes fresh twist.

text.p: A sensational serial murder case, reopened last month by Italy's highest court, took a fresh twist on Thursday when a prosecution witness was reported to have admitted killing two of the 16 victims.

Giancarlo Lotti, a 57-year-old labourer who has been living at a secret location under police protection, told magistrates that he had shot dead two German tourists in 1983, the Italian news agency ANSA reported.

ANSA said Lotti made his confession on December 23 but his lawyer Alessandro Falciani said no interrogation had taken place on that day and "categorically denied" that his client had admitted to murder.
The Germans, Horst Meyer and Uwe Jeans Rusch, both 24, were shot as they slept in a camper van in the Tuscan countryside.

Investigators believe the killer or killers mistook the men for a courting couple. Eight double killings were committed in the area between 1968 and 1985 in what Italian media have dubbed the "Monster of Florence" murders.

The Court of Cassation, Italy's highest court, last month ordered the retrial of Pietro Pacciani, an elderly farmer convicted two years ago of seven of the double murders but then dramatically cleared on appeal.

Lotti had previously maintained that he simply acted as look-out and driver for Pacciani and another man, Mario Vanni, who has been held in jail since last February after Lotti's allegations that he had also taken part in the killings.

A third man, Giovanni Faggi, has been released from jail but is also under investigation. Prosecutors are due to decide shortly whether to send Lotti, Faggi and Vanni to trial for conspiracy in the "Monster" murder case.
Pacciani, who is in his 70s, has always maintained his innocence.
